```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# eval = FALSE so this template knits as a reference without running.
# In a real project, delete this line or set eval = TRUE.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# How to use this template

**Placeholders.** Replace each one with your own names:

| Placeholder | What it stands for |
|---|---|
| `shapefile1`, `shapefile2` | polygon layers (sf), e.g. boroughs, wards |
| `points1` | point layer (sf), e.g. plaques, hotels |
| `df1`, `df2` | tables read from a CSV |
| `raster1` | single-layer raster (terra SpatRaster) |
| `rasterstack1` | multi-layer raster |
| `shp_id` / `df_id` | the shared ID column in the spatial layer / the table (e.g. `GSS_CODE` / `new_code`) |
| `name_col` | area name column |
| `var1`, `var2` | numeric columns you're analysing |
| `group_col` | a category column |
| `dep_var`, `ind_var1`, `ind_var2` | regression variables |
| `"data"`, `"file1.shp"` | your folder and file names |

**Order of a project.** Not every project needs every step. Most need steps 0–7; steps 8–10 are the analysis method you choose.

0. Set up packages and paths
1. Read in data
2. Check and clean attributes
3. Check and match CRS
4. Join tables to spatial data (attribute join)
5. Spatial operations (subset, spatial join, counts, raster crop/mask/extract)
6. Descriptive statistics and charts
7. Map design
8. Point pattern analysis (P6)
9. Spatial autocorrelation (P7)
10. Regression and spatial regression (P8)
11. Save outputs

`(P#)` marks the practical a chunk comes from. Lines marked `(not in practicals)` are small extras.

---

# 0. Set up

```{r packages}
# install once in the console (not in the Rmd):
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "sf", "terra", "tidyterra", "tmap", "tmaptools", "here", "janitor", "fs"))

library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, readr, tidyr, ggplot2, stringr, tibble
library(sf)          # vector data
library(terra)       # raster data
library(tidyterra)   # tidyverse verbs + ggplot2 for rasters
library(tmap)        # maps
library(tmaptools)   # read_osm basemaps
library(here)        # file paths from the project folder
library(janitor)     # clean_names
library(fs)          # dir_info

# load only what the project needs:
# library(plotly)                                   # interactive charts (P3)
# library(classInt)                                 # class breaks (P5)
# library(grid)                                     # placing maps/charts on one page (P5)
# library(spatstat); library(sp); library(fpc); library(dbscan); library(ggspatial)   # point patterns (P6)
# library(spdep); library(RColorBrewer)             # spatial autocorrelation (P7)
# library(broom); library(car); library(corrr); library(performance)
# library(spatialreg); library(lmtest); library(spgwr)                                # regression (P8)

# terra and other packages can mask dplyr verbs:
# the course writes dplyr::select(), dplyr::filter() to be safe
```

---

# 1. Read in data

## 1a. Vector data: shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON (P1, P3, P6)

```{r read-vector}
# shapefile: point to the .shp (the .dbf, .shx and .prj must be in the same folder)
shapefile1 <- st_read(here("data", "folder", "file1.shp"))

# GeoPackage: list the layers first, then pick one
st_layers(here("data", "file1.gpkg"))
shapefile1 <- st_read(here("data", "file1.gpkg"), layer = "layer_name")

# GeoJSON: local file or URL
points1 <- st_read(here("data", "file2.geojson"))
```

## 1b. CSV: local or from the web (P1, P2, P8)

```{r read-csv}
# local file
df1 <- read_csv(here("data", "file1.csv"))

# from the web:
# - encoding = "latin1" stops symbols like £ breaking column names
# - na = ... tells R which text means "missing", so numeric columns stay numeric
df1 <- read_csv("https://web-address/file1.csv",
                locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                na = c("", "NA", "n/a")) %>%
  clean_names()   # lowercase_with_underscores, no spaces/symbols

# force column types if read_csv guesses wrong (e.g. codes read as numbers)
df1 <- read_csv(here("data", "file1.csv"),
                col_types = cols(df_id = col_character(),
                                 var1 = col_number(),
                                 var2 = col_number()))
```

## 1c. CSV with coordinates → points (P5, P8)

```{r read-csv-points}
points1 <- read_csv(here("data", "file_xy.csv")) %>%
  # x = longitude, y = latitude; crs = the CRS the coordinates are written in
  st_as_sf(., coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(., 27700) %>%                   # reproject (see step 3)
  filter(type_col == "value")                  # optional: keep only what you need
```

## 1d. Raster: single file or a stack from a folder (P3, P4)

```{r read-raster}
# single raster
raster1 <- terra::rast(here("data", "file1.tif"))
raster1          # prints extent, resolution, CRS, layer names
plot(raster1)

# several .tif files from one folder → one multi-layer stack
listfiles <- dir_info(here("data")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(path, ".tif")) %>%
  dplyr::select(path) %>%
  pull()

rasterstack1 <- listfiles %>%
  terra::rast()

rasterstack1[[1]]                              # first layer
names(rasterstack1) <- c("layer1", "layer2", "layer3")   # one name per layer (e.g. months)
rasterstack1 %>% tidyterra::select(layer1)     # pick a layer by name
```

## 1e. Download and unzip from the web (P8)

```{r download-unzip}
download.file("https://web-address/file.zip",
              destfile = here("data", "file.zip"))

dir_info(here("data")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(path, ".zip")) %>%
  dplyr::select(path) %>%
  pull() %>%
  as.character() %>%
  utils::unzip(exdir = here("data"))
```

## 1f. First look (P1)

```{r first-look}
summary(shapefile1)                    # columns, ranges, CRS
head(df1, n = 10)                      # first rows
shapefile1 %>% st_geometry() %>% plot()   # outline only
qtm(shapefile1)                        # quick tmap
```

---

# 2. Check and clean attributes

## 2a. Check column types (P2, P7, P8)

```{r check-types}
# numbers stored as "character" usually mean text like "n/a" in the column → fix the na = argument in read_csv
Datatypelist <- df1 %>%
  summarise_all(class) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "All_variables",
               values_to = "Variable_class")
Datatypelist

# for an sf layer, drop the geometry first
shapefile1 %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% summarise_all(class)
```

## 2b. Clean and subset (P2, P6)

```{r clean-subset}
shapefile1 <- shapefile1 %>%
  clean_names() %>%                                    # tidy column names
  filter(str_detect(shp_id, "^E09")) %>%               # keep rows whose code starts with E09 (London boroughs)
  dplyr::select(shp_id, name_col, var1, var2) %>%      # keep the columns you need (contains("text") also works)
  dplyr::rename(new_name = old_name)                   # rename: new = old

points1 <- distinct(points1)                           # remove duplicate points/rows (P6)

df1 <- df1 %>%
  mutate(group_col = as.factor(group_col))             # categories → factor (P8)
```

---

# 3. Check and match CRS

All layers must share a CRS before any overlay, join, crop or distance calculation.

**Common CRS codes**
- **27700:** British National Grid, in metres. Use it for UK areas, distances and point patterns.
- **4326:** WGS84 latitude/longitude, used by GPS and web basemaps.
- **3112:** an Australian projection (P3).

## 3a. Vector (P3, P5)

```{r crs-vector}
st_crs(shapefile1)               # full CRS info
st_crs(shapefile1)$epsg          # just the EPSG code

# st_set_crs: ONLY when the CRS is missing (NA). It labels the data, it does NOT move coordinates
shapefile1 <- shapefile1 %>% st_set_crs(., 4326)

# st_transform: reprojects (recalculates coordinates) into a new CRS
shapefile1 <- shapefile1 %>% st_transform(., 27700)
points1    <- points1 %>% st_transform(., 27700)
```

## 3b. Raster (P3)

```{r crs-raster}
crs(raster1)                                   # check

raster1_proj <- raster1 %>%
  terra::project(., "EPSG:27700")              # reproject a raster
# P3 uses proj4 strings too, e.g. Mollweide:
# terra::project(raster1, "+proj=moll +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")

# often simpler: reproject the VECTOR to match the raster before crop/mask/extract
shapefile1_r <- shapefile1 %>% st_transform(., crs(raster1))
```

## 3c. sf ↔ sp (P3, P6)

```{r sf-sp}
# some older packages need sp objects
shapefile1_sp <- shapefile1 %>% as(., "Spatial")   # sf → sp
shapefile1_sf <- shapefile1_sp %>% st_as_sf()       # sp → sf
```

---

# 4. Join a table to spatial data (attribute join) (P1, P2, P7, P8)

```{r join-checks}
# BEFORE JOINING
# 1. Find the unique ID that exists in BOTH (e.g. GSS code). Column names can differ; values and type must match
# 2. Check the ID is unique in the table: duplicates multiply rows in the result
df1 %>% count(df_id) %>% filter(n > 1)          # any rows returned = duplicate IDs
# 3. Both IDs should be the same type (usually character, e.g. "E09000001"); see step 2a
# 4. clean_names() renames columns (e.g. "New code" → new_code): use the cleaned name in by =
# 5. Put the sf layer on the LEFT so the result stays spatial
```

```{r join-attribute}
joined1 <- shapefile1 %>%
  left_join(., df1, by = c("shp_id" = "df_id"))  # c("name in left" = "name in right")

# which join?
# left_join:  keeps ALL features in shapefile1; no match → NA. Usual choice
# inner_join: keeps only features with a match in both; unmatched areas disappear from the map
# right_join: keeps all rows of df1; rows without a match get empty geometry. Rarely wanted
# merge(shapefile1, df1, by.x = "shp_id", by.y = "df_id") is the base R version (P1)
```

```{r join-after}
# AFTER JOINING: check it worked
nrow(shapefile1); nrow(joined1)               # should match for left_join; more rows = duplicate IDs

joined1 <- joined1 %>%
  distinct(shp_id, .keep_all = TRUE)          # remove duplicated features (P2, P7)

summary(joined1$var1)                         # lots of NAs = IDs didn't match

# (not in practicals) list table rows that found no match
df1 %>% anti_join(st_drop_geometry(shapefile1), by = c("df_id" = "shp_id"))

qtm(joined1, fill = "var1")                   # quick map to eyeball the join (P8)
```

---

# 5. Spatial operations

## 5a. Select by location / clip points to an area (P6, P7)

```{r spatial-subset}
# both layers must share a CRS (step 3)
points1_sub <- points1[shapefile1, ]         # keep points inside the polygons ("select by location")

area1 <- shapefile1 %>% filter(name_col == "Area1")   # select by attribute: one area
points1_area <- points1[area1, ]

st_intersects(shapefile1, points1_sub)       # which points fall in which polygon (row numbers)
```

## 5b. Spatial join (P5)

```{r spatial-join}
# st_join attaches attributes by LOCATION (no shared ID needed). Order matters:

# polygons first → one row per point inside each polygon (polygons repeated)
joined_sp <- st_join(shapefile1, points1)
joined_sum <- joined_sp %>%
  group_by(shp_id, name_col) %>%
  summarise(count = n())
# NOTE (P5): polygons with 0 points still show count = 1 here (the NA row). Use 5c for true counts

# points first → each point gets the attributes of the polygon it sits in
points1_attr <- st_join(points1, shapefile1)
```

## 5c. Count points per polygon and density (P5, P7)

```{r point-in-polygon}
counts1 <- shapefile1 %>%
  mutate(n_points = lengths(st_intersects(., points1))) %>%  # count points per polygon (P5 uses st_contains)
  mutate(area = st_area(.)) %>%                              # m² when the CRS is in metres
  mutate(density = n_points / area) %>%                      # points per m²
  clean_names()
```

## 5d. Vector geoprocessing (P3, P5, P6, P7)

```{r vector-geoprocessing}
shapefile1_simple <- shapefile1 %>% st_simplify(., dTolerance = 1000)   # fewer vertices, draws faster

bbox1 <- c(xmin = 0, ymin = 0, xmax = 100000, ymax = 100000)            # in the layer's CRS units
shapefile1_crop <- shapefile1$geometry %>% st_crop(., bbox1)            # cut to a rectangle

centroids1 <- shapefile1 %>% st_centroid() %>% st_geometry()            # centre point of each polygon
```

## 5e. Raster: crop, mask, extract (P3)

```{r raster-crop-mask}
raster1_crop <- terra::crop(raster1, shapefile1_r)       # cut to the vector's bounding box
raster1_mask <- terra::mask(raster1_crop, shapefile1_r)  # cells outside the exact outline → NA
plot(raster1_mask)
```

```{r raster-extract}
# values at points from a table of coordinates (same CRS as the raster)
site <- c("Site1", "Site2", "Site3")
lon  <- c(0.00, 0.00, 0.00)
lat  <- c(0.00, 0.00, 0.00)
samples <- data.frame(site, lon, lat, row.names = "site")

vals1 <- terra::extract(rasterstack1, samples) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  add_column(Site = site, .before = 1)

# or from an sf point layer
vals1 <- terra::extract(rasterstack1, points1)
```

---

# 6. Descriptive statistics and charts

## 6a. Summary statistics (P3, P5)

```{r desc-summary}
summary(joined1)                                   # quick overview of every column

stats1 <- joined1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%                           # stats run on tables, not geometry
  dplyr::select(var1, var2) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(min = min, max = max, mean = mean,
                                      median = median, sd = sd)))
# NAs make these return NA: remove them first with drop_na()
```

## 6b. Reshape to long format (P3, P5)

```{r desc-pivot}
# long format = one column of names + one column of values; needed for grouped stats/plots
df_long <- df1 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(var1, var2),               # or cols = 1:12
               names_to = "variable",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  drop_na()
```

## 6c. Grouped statistics (P3)

```{r desc-grouped}
grouped1 <- df_long %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%                           # one row per group
  summarise(mean  = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd    = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min   = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max   = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR   = IQR(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            count = n())

overall1 <- df_long %>%                            # one figure for the whole dataset
  summarise(mean_all = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE))

head(grouped1, n = 1)
```

## 6d. New variables and comparisons (P2)

```{r desc-derived}
df1 <- df1 %>%
  mutate(avg = (var1 + var2) / 2) %>%                          # average of two columns
  mutate(normalised = avg / mean(avg)) %>%                     # relative to the mean
  mutate(diff = avg - 81.16) %>%                               # difference from a reference value
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3)) %>%              # round every numeric column
  mutate(compare = case_when(avg > 81.16 ~ "above average",    # label by condition
                             TRUE ~ "below average"))

df1 %>% arrange(desc(normalised)) %>% slice_head(n = 5)       # top 5
```

## 6e. Distribution charts (P3, P5, P8)

```{r desc-hist-base}
# quick base R histogram with set breaks
hist(df1$var1,
     breaks = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 40),
     col = "red",
     main = "Histogram title",
     xlab = "x label",
     ylab = "Frequency")
```

```{r desc-hist-ggplot}
# histogram + dashed mean line
ggplot(df1, aes(x = var1)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean(var1, na.rm = TRUE)),
             color = "blue", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Title", x = "x label", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))   # centre the title

# histogram + density curve (P8): checks the shape of the distribution (normal? skewed?)
ggplot(df1, aes(x = var1)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = 5) +   # P8 writes ..density.. (older syntax)
  geom_density(colour = "red", linewidth = 1, adjust = 1)
```

```{r desc-hist-groups}
# two groups overlaid, each with its mean line
means1 <- df_long %>% group_by(variable) %>% summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(df_long, aes(x = value, color = variable, fill = variable)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(data = means1, aes(xintercept = mean, color = variable), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Title", x = "x label", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic()

# one panel per group
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", binwidth = 5) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ .)
```

```{r desc-violin}
# violin plot: distribution shape per group (P5)
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = variable, y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, color = "grey30", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("var1" = "Label 1", "var2" = "Label 2")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r desc-plotly}
# interactive overlaid histogram (P3)
library(plotly)
g1 <- df_long %>% filter(variable == "var1")
g2 <- df_long %>% filter(variable == "var2")

plot_ly(alpha = 0.6) %>%
  add_histogram(x = g1$value, xbins = list(start = 0, end = 40, size = 2.5), name = "Var 1") %>%
  add_histogram(x = g2$value, xbins = list(start = 0, end = 40, size = 2.5), name = "Var 2") %>%
  layout(barmode = "overlay",
         xaxis = list(title = "x label"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Frequency"))
```

```{r desc-scatter}
# scatter plot + straight-line fit (P8)
ggplot(df1, aes(x = var1, y = var2)) +
  geom_point() +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1)
```

## 6f. Raster statistics (P3)

```{r desc-raster}
hist(raster1_mask[[1]], col = "red", main = "Layer 1")   # quick histogram of one layer

rasterdf1 <- raster1_mask %>% as.data.frame()            # one row per cell, one column per layer

raster_long <- rasterdf1 %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "layer", values_to = "value") %>%
  drop_na()

raster_stats1 <- raster_long %>%                         # stats per layer, as in 6c
  group_by(layer) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(value), sd = sd(value), min = min(value), max = max(value))

# raster on a map with ggplot (tidyterra)
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = raster1_mask, aes(fill = layer1))
```

## 6g. Class breaks for maps (P5)

```{r desc-breaks}
library(classInt)
breaks1 <- joined1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pull(var1) %>%                                  # needs a vector, not a table
  classIntervals(., n = 5, style = "jenks")       # also "quantile", "equal", "sd"
breaks1$brks                                      # use in tm_scale_intervals(breaks = breaks1$brks)
```

---

# 7. Map design (tmap)

```{r map-mode}
tmap_mode("plot")   # static map: use for reports
# tmap_mode("view") # interactive map: use for exploring
```

## 7a. Full choropleth (P2, P5, P7)

```{r map-choropleth}
map1 <- tm_shape(joined1) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "var1",
              col = "black", lwd = 0.5,                      # border colour and width
              fill_alpha = 0.8,                              # transparency
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
                values = "brewer.bu_pu",                     # palette (browse: cols4all::c4a_gui())
                n = 5,
                style = "jenks"),                            # or style = "fixed", breaks = breaks1$brks
              fill.legend = tm_legend(
                title = "Legend title",
                title.size = 0.85, size = 0.8,
                position = tm_pos_out("right", "center", pos.v = "center")),  # legend outside the map
              fill.chart = tm_chart_violin()) +              # optional: distribution chart under the legend
  tm_compass(type = "arrow", position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_title("Map title", size = 2, position = c("center", "top")) +
  tm_credits("Data: source", size = 0.6)
map1
```

## 7b. Points and labels over polygons (P5, P6)

```{r map-points}
tm_shape(shapefile1) +
  tm_polygons(fill_alpha = 0.5) +            # or tm_borders(col = "darkblue") for outlines only
tm_shape(points1) +
  tm_dots(fill = "blue", size = 0.1)
# styled points with labels:
#  tm_symbols(shape = 20, fill = "orange", col = "black", size = 0.8) +
#  tm_text("name_col", xmod = -1, ymod = -0.5)
```

## 7c. Side-by-side maps sharing one legend (P5)

```{r map-facets}
map_facets <- tm_shape(joined1) +
  tm_polygons(fill = c("var1", "var2"),                     # one map per column
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.blues", breaks = breaks1$brks),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Legend title"),
              fill.free = FALSE) +                          # FALSE = shared legend
  tm_facets(nrow = 2) +
  tm_layout(panel.labels = c("Label 1", "Label 2"), panel.show = TRUE)
map_facets
```

## 7d. Basemaps (P2)

```{r map-basemap-static}
# static: download tiles for the layer's extent, draw as an RGB raster
basemap1 <- shapefile1 %>%
  st_bbox(.) %>%
  tmaptools::read_osm(., type = "esri", zoom = NULL)

tm_shape(basemap1) + tm_rgb() +
tm_shape(joined1) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "var1", fill_alpha = 0.5)
```

```{r map-basemap-interactive}
# interactive: P2 transforms to 4326 first
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(st_transform(joined1, 4326)) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "var1", fill_alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_basemap(server = "OpenStreetMap")
tmap_mode("plot")
```

## 7e. Inset map and saving (P5)

```{r map-inset}
# 1. locator map: wider area, outlined box showing the study area
studyarea_box <- st_bbox(joined1, crs = st_crs(joined1)) %>%
  st_as_sfc()                                                # bbox → polygon

locator1 <- tm_shape(shapefile2) +                           # e.g. country outline
  tm_polygons(col = "darkslategray1") +
  tm_shape(studyarea_box) +
  tm_borders(col = "grey40", lwd = 3) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE, bg.color = "transparent")

# 2. add it as an inset to the main map
inset1 <- tmap_grob(locator1, asp = 1.1)
final_map <- map1 + tm_inset(inset1, position = tm_pos_out("right", "center"))

# 3. save
tmap_save(final_map, here("outputs", "map1.png"),
          width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

```{r map-with-chart}
# put a map and a ggplot chart on one page (P5)
library(grid)
png(here("outputs", "map_chart.png"), width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)
map1
print(chart1, vp = viewport(x = 0.67, y = 0.83, width = 0.25, height = 0.35))   # chart1 = a saved ggplot
dev.off()
```

## 7f. ggplot2 alternative (P3, P6)

```{r map-ggplot}
library(ggspatial)
ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(zoom = 13) +                       # basemap tiles
  geom_sf(data = joined1, aes(fill = var1), alpha = 0.7, color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = points1, size = 1) +
  theme_bw()
# rasters: ggplot() + geom_spatraster(data = raster1, aes(fill = layer1))
```

---

# 8. Point pattern analysis (P6)

Use this for "are these points clustered?". Work in a metre-based CRS (e.g. 27700).

```{r ppp-setup}
library(spatstat); library(sp)

area1 <- shapefile1 %>% filter(name_col == "Area1")      # study area
points1_area <- distinct(points1)[area1, ]                # remove duplicates, clip to area

window1 <- as.owin(area1)                                 # study-area boundary for spatstat

points1_sp <- points1_area %>% as(., "Spatial")           # sf → sp
points1.ppp <- ppp(x = points1_sp@coords[, 1],
                   y = points1_sp@coords[, 2],
                   window = window1)
plot(points1.ppp, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, main = "Title")
```

```{r ppp-kde}
# kernel density: sigma = smoothing distance in CRS units (try several)
points1.ppp %>% density(., sigma = 500) %>% plot()
```

```{r ppp-quadrat}
# quadrat test: H0 = complete spatial randomness (CSR)
# p < 0.05 → reject CSR (pattern is clustered or dispersed)
# P6 also builds the observed vs expected Poisson comparison by hand
teststats1 <- quadrat.test(points1.ppp, nx = 6, ny = 6)
plot(points1.ppp, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
plot(teststats1, add = TRUE, col = "red")
teststats1
```

```{r ppp-ripley}
# Ripley's K: observed line ABOVE the red CSR line = clustering at that distance; below = dispersed
K1 <- points1.ppp %>% Kest(., correction = "border") %>% plot()
Kval1 <- as.data.frame(Kest(points1.ppp, correction = "Ripley"))   # values as a table
```

```{r ppp-dbscan}
# DBSCAN: finds WHERE the clusters are
library(fpc); library(dbscan)
points1_xy <- points1_sp %>% coordinates(.) %>% as.data.frame()

points1_xy %>% dbscan::kNNdistplot(., k = 4)   # choose eps at the "knee" of the curve; k = MinPts

db1 <- points1_xy %>% fpc::dbscan(., eps = 700, MinPts = 4)
# eps = search radius (CRS units); MinPts = minimum points per cluster
points1_xy <- points1_xy %>% mutate(dbcluster = db1$cluster)   # 0 = noise
```

```{r ppp-hulls-map}
points1_clusters <- st_as_sf(points1_xy, coords = c("coords.x1", "coords.x2"), crs = 27700)

hulls1 <- points1_clusters %>%
  filter(dbcluster > 0) %>%                         # drop noise points
  group_by(dbcluster) %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_combine(geometry)) %>%    # combine each cluster's points
  mutate(geometry = st_convex_hull(geometry)) %>%   # draw a polygon around them
  st_as_sf()

library(ggspatial)
ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(zoom = 13) +
  geom_sf(data = points1_clusters, aes(color = dbcluster), size = 3) +
  geom_sf(data = hulls1, aes(fill = dbcluster), alpha = 0.8, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_bw()
```

---

# 9. Spatial autocorrelation (P7)

Use this for "do similar values sit near each other?". It needs polygon values: use the densities from 5c, or a variable joined in step 4.

```{r autocorr-neighbours}
library(spdep)

# keep one row per area (P7)
counts1 <- counts1 %>%
  group_by(shp_id) %>%
  summarise(density = first(density), name = first(name_col), count = first(n_points))

coords1 <- counts1 %>% st_centroid() %>% st_geometry()

# neighbours: queen = polygons sharing an edge OR corner
nb1 <- counts1 %>% poly2nb(., queen = TRUE)
summary(nb1)                                   # average number of neighbours
# or k nearest neighbours (P8)
knn1 <- coords1 %>% knearneigh(., k = 4) %>% knn2nb()

plot(nb1, st_geometry(coords1), col = "red")
plot(counts1$geometry, add = TRUE)

# spatial weights
lw1 <- nb1 %>% nb2listw(., style = "C")
# style: "B" = binary, "W" = row standardised (each row sums to 1), "C" = globally standardised
```

```{r autocorr-global}
# Global Moran's I: +1 clustered, 0 random, -1 dispersed
I_global <- counts1 %>% pull(density) %>% as.vector() %>% moran.test(., lw1)

# Geary's C: < 1 similar values cluster, 1 = none, > 1 dissimilar values cluster
C_global <- counts1 %>% pull(density) %>% as.vector() %>% geary.test(., lw1)

# Getis-Ord General G: G > expected → high values cluster (hot spots); < expected → low values cluster
G_global <- counts1 %>% pull(density) %>% as.vector() %>% globalG.test(., lw1)

I_global; C_global; G_global
```

```{r autocorr-local}
# Local Moran's I and Gi* for each area
I_local <- counts1 %>% pull(density) %>% as.vector() %>% localmoran(., lw1) %>% as_tibble()
Gi_local <- counts1 %>% pull(density) %>% as.vector() %>% localG(., lw1)

# attach z-scores without re-sorting counts1 in between (row order must match)
counts1 <- counts1 %>%
  mutate(density_I  = as.numeric(I_local$Ii),
         density_Iz = as.numeric(I_local$Z.Ii),
         density_G  = as.numeric(Gi_local))
```

```{r autocorr-map}
# z-score breaks: ±1.65 = 90%, ±1.96 = 95%, ±2.58 = 99% significance
breaks_z <- c(-1000, -2.58, -1.96, -1.65, 1.65, 1.96, 2.58, 1000)

tm_shape(counts1) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "density_Iz",                 # or "density_G" for Gi* hot/cold spots
              fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.br_bg",   # diverging palette
                                              midpoint = "NA",
                                              style = "fixed",
                                              breaks = breaks_z),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Local Moran's I (z-score)",
                                      position = tm_pos_out("right", "center", pos.v = "center")))
```

---

# 10. Regression and spatial regression (P8)

## 10a. Explore and transform

```{r reg-explore}
reg_data <- joined1 %>% clean_names()

# distributions: aim for roughly normal; skewed → try a transformation
ggplot(reg_data, aes(x = ind_var1)) + geom_histogram()
ggplot(reg_data, aes(x = log(ind_var1))) + geom_histogram()

library(car)
symbox(~ind_var1, reg_data, na.rm = TRUE, powers = seq(-3, 3, by = .5))   # compares transformations: pick the most symmetric

ggplot(reg_data, aes(x = ind_var1, y = dep_var)) + geom_point()           # linear relationship?
```

## 10b. OLS model

```{r reg-ols}
library(broom)
model1 <- lm(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2), data = reg_data)

summary(model1)
tidy(model1)       # coefficients and p-values as a table
glance(model1)     # R², adjusted R², AIC

model_data1 <- model1 %>% augment(., reg_data)   # adds fitted values and residuals
reg_data <- reg_data %>% mutate(model1_resids = residuals(model1))
```

## 10c. Check assumptions

```{r reg-assumptions}
# 1. Residuals roughly normal
ggplot(model_data1, aes(x = .resid)) + geom_histogram()

# 2. No multicollinearity: correlations < 0.8; VIF < 10
library(corrr)
reg_data %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(dep_var, ind_var1, ind_var2) %>%
  correlate() %>%
  rplot()
vif(model1)

# 3. Equal variance (homoscedasticity): no funnel shape in residuals vs fitted
par(mfrow = c(2, 2)); plot(model1)
library(performance); check_model(model1, check = "all")

# 4. Independent errors: Durbin-Watson about 2 = OK
durbinWatsonTest(model1) %>% tidy()
```

## 10d. Are the residuals spatially autocorrelated?

```{r reg-resid-moran}
qtm(reg_data, fill = "model1_resids")                     # map the residuals

coords_r <- reg_data %>% st_centroid() %>% st_geometry()
nb_r  <- reg_data %>% poly2nb(., queen = TRUE)
knn_r <- coords_r %>% knearneigh(., k = 4) %>% knn2nb()
lw_queen <- nb_r  %>% nb2listw(., style = "W")
lw_knn   <- knn_r %>% nb2listw(., style = "W")

# significant Moran's I on the residuals → spatial model needed
reg_data %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% pull(model1_resids) %>% moran.test(., lw_queen) %>% tidy()
reg_data %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% pull(model1_resids) %>% moran.test(., lw_knn) %>% tidy()
```

## 10e. Lag or error model?

```{r reg-lm-tests}
# Lagrange multiplier tests: compare LMerr vs LMlag; if both are significant, use the robust (R) versions
lm.LMtests(model1, lw_queen, test = c("LMerr", "LMlag", "RLMerr", "RLMlag", "SARMA"))
```

```{r reg-spatial-lag}
# spatial lag: the dependent variable in neighbouring areas affects each area
library(spatialreg)
slag1 <- lagsarlm(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2),
                  data = reg_data,
                  nb2listw(nb_r, style = "C"),
                  method = "eigen")
tidy(slag1); glance(slag1)        # rho = strength of the spatial lag

library(lmtest)
lrtest(slag1, model1)             # significant → lag model fits better than OLS

impacts(slag1, listw = nb2listw(nb_r, style = "C"))   # direct, indirect and total effects
```

```{r reg-spatial-error}
# spatial error: the residuals are spatially correlated (unmeasured spatial factor)
sem1 <- errorsarlm(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2),
                   data = reg_data,
                   nb2listw(knn_r, style = "C"),
                   method = "eigen")
tidy(sem1)                        # lambda = strength of the spatial error
```

## 10f. Dummy (categorical) variables

```{r reg-dummy}
reg_data <- reg_data %>%
  mutate(group_col = as.factor(group_col)) %>%
  mutate(group_col = relevel(group_col, ref = "Reference level"))   # choose the baseline category
contrasts(reg_data$group_col)

model2 <- lm(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2) + group_col, data = reg_data)
tidy(model2)
```

## 10g. Geographically weighted regression (GWR)

```{r reg-gwr}
# GWR: lets coefficients vary across space
library(spgwr)
coords_xy <- st_coordinates(coords_r)
reg_data2 <- cbind(reg_data, coords_xy)                  # adds X and Y columns

bw1 <- gwr.sel(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2),
               data = reg_data2,
               coords = cbind(reg_data2$X, reg_data2$Y),
               adapt = TRUE)                            # adaptive bandwidth

gwr1 <- gwr(dep_var ~ ind_var1 + log(ind_var2),
            data = reg_data2,
            coords = cbind(reg_data2$X, reg_data2$Y),
            adapt = bw1, hatmatrix = TRUE, se.fit = TRUE)
gwr1

results1 <- as.data.frame(gwr1$SDF)
names(results1)                                         # find the coefficient column names

reg_data2 <- reg_data %>%
  mutate(coef_ind1 = results1$ind_var1,
         # significance: |coefficient| - 2 * SE > 0 → significant at about 95%
         sig_ind1 = abs(gwr1$SDF$ind_var1) - 2 * gwr1$SDF$ind_var1_se)

tm_shape(reg_data2) +
  tm_polygons("coef_ind1", fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.rd_bu"), fill_alpha = 0.5)
```

# 11. Save outputs (P1, P5)

```{r save-outputs}
# map image
tmap_save(map1, here("outputs", "map1.png"), width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# spatial data to a GeoPackage (delete_dsn = TRUE overwrites the whole file)
joined1 %>% st_write(., here("outputs", "project.gpkg"),
                     layer = "joined1", delete_dsn = TRUE)

# add a plain table to the same GeoPackage
library(RSQLite)
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = here("outputs", "project.gpkg"))
con %>% dbListTables()
con %>% dbWriteTable(., "df1_table", df1, overwrite = TRUE)
con %>% dbDisconnect()                                   # always close the connection
```
